tara-cs: quick sync - BlueWave is stuck on onboarding. Their node SDK init from corporate VPN returns 403 on /v1/embeddings, but same token works from home. they sent a sanitized curl and say token has correct scopes.

alex-eng: usually a middlebox. ask them for curl -v output and the decoded JWT claims (aud/scope/iss/exp). proxies sometimes break header casing or inject a proxy auth header. also confirm whether they use an internal WAF that rewrites paths.

ops-sam: add two checks: 1) rate-limiter fingerprints on our edge sometimes return 403-like responses when a burst hits an untagged tenant; 2) corporate TLS interception often replaces certs which can change SNI/Host - our auth checks may fail if aud is host-bound. can they run: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings` from inside corp and paste output?

tara-cs: they pasted this sanitized repro: ```curl -i https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer eyJ...redacted" -d '{"input":"test"}' HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden content-type: application/json {"error":"invalid_scope","message":"token lacks scope: embeddings.create"}``` they insist scope exists and that the same token works from outside the VPN.

alex-eng: if the same opaque token works externally but not internally, it's almost certainly altered in transit. ask them to: 1) decode the JWT on jwt.io and copy aud/scope (they can redact sub/iss) 2) run `openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -servername api.redwood.ai` from a corp host to see the presented cert chain (if they get a corp cert, it's MITM).

ops-sam: also request `traceroute api.redwood.ai` and `curl -v` so we can correlate with our edge logs. include any `x-request-id` or `x-redwood-*` headers from the 403. if they can't share full pcap, a plain terminal curl is sufficient to show header truncation.

onboard-bot: Helpful guide: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdks/node#network-compatibility — section on proxies, header rewriting, and ephemeral-token caveats. If company policy forbids sharing, they can paste the decoded claims and the first/last 8 chars of the token instead.

tara-cs: i've asked for: curl -v from corp and from remote, decoded claims, cert chain, and any request-id. flagged as high priority for renewal risk. will update once they respond. :eyes:

alex-eng: if they come back with a corp cert and header differences, we can recommend a small workaround: use a short-lived server-side mint (proxy token) so the browser only talks to their own backend and avoids corp VPN rules. note that requires a quick change to redirect token fetches.

ops-sam: note for CS playbook: add a checklist entry for "verify TLS interception" and "compare curl -v headers inside vs outside network". saves time on these recurring cases.

tara-cs: thanks — logging this under the account health thread. will ping here when artifacts arrive. :thumbsup:
